thread:
lena (AE): Heads-up: SableBank is pushing for a Q1 enterprise commit. Traffic profile: 480 rps peak, ~14k tokens/session, sustained 75m market window with micro-spikes before/after. They want p50 < 220ms during the window and >99.9% uptime for that interval. Asking for a concrete reserved GPU + burst credits proposal and an ops handoff (preheat, KMS checks, canary).

carlos (Sales Eng): 480 rps @14k tokens — big KV footprint but less than some other deals. Important: do they accept quantized int8/int4? That materially changes GPU count.

lena (AE): Procurement prefers quantized for cost but legal requires a fallback to fp16 model for high-risk flows. Also they require KMS + HSM notes.

anya (Solutions): Proposed quick sketch: baseline 4 reserved GPUs (quantized) tuned for low latency, 2 burst GPUs available via burst credits which can be prewarmed on schedule. Configure persistent KV cache with per-tenant namespaces and 12h TTL. If they want fp16 baseline, bump baseline -> 9 GPUs.

vik (SRE): Back-of-envelope calc: assume our runtime achieves ~0.14 tokens/ms per A100-equivalent on long context for quantized variant. For 480 rps * 14k tokens = 6.72M tokens/minute. That equals ~48k tokens/sec. At 0.14 tokens/ms per GPU (140 tokens/sec), need ~343 GPUs — that sounds wrong; let me break it down: tokens/sec per GPU = 0.14 tokens/ms * 1000 ms/s = 140 tokens/s. For 48k tokens/s, GPUs = 48,000 / 140 ≈ 343. Hmm — that's unrealistic; this tells us my per-GPU throughput assumption is off for long-ctx sessions because KV cache reduces work per request. With prefix KV caching and batching we can amortize prompt cost; practical perf testing needed. Until perf runs, recommend conservative reserve of 10 quantized GPUs + 4 burst slots for safety.

morgan (Infra): Private VPC requested. Note: Private + AZ spread for SLA means we must reserve capacity in customer's AZs; this limits our ability to burst into the shared pool. Lead time: 2-4 weeks for infra provisioning and KMS/HSM integration testing.

carlos (Sales Eng): Procurement asks for monthly cost estimate and worst-case overage. Can we produce a sample amortized $/token for quantized vs fp16? CFO meeting tomorrow.

anya (Solutions): Quick conservative ballpark: quantify two scenarios in the quote: (A) Quantized baseline 10 GPUs reserved + 4 burst GPUs, monthly burst credit 250k tokens. (B) FP16 baseline 24 GPUs reserved + 6 burst GPUs. Use a 2.6x efficiency factor for quantized in the table. I'll draft the two-line pricing.

vik (SRE): Real action: need perf runs on their model (they provided model id: redwood-compat-13b-rf) at 2 context lengths: 4k and 14k, and a set of 20 representative prompts. If they supply container + samples by EOD we can bench in 24h. Until then we must be conservative.

morgan (Infra): KMS checklist for the runbook: service account with decrypt rights to the key, network path open to KMS endpoints during prewarm, HSM cert thumbprint exchange, and rotation window documented. I'll add these as an explicit pre-deploy checklist.

carlos (Sales Eng): Ops question from their SRE: how do we prewarm KV for the 75m window without incurring full token bill for warmups?

anya (Solutions): Prewarm pattern: run a scheduled prewarm job that issues synthetic warm requests for high-frequency prefixes only (not full 14k prompts). Use a staged warm that primes KV entries and a short tail warm during first 5 minutes of market open. Add KV persistence so repeated warmups are cheap. We'll include a prewarm cron example in runbook.

vik (SRE): Example autoscale snippet for handoff (ops-config):
```
autoscale_policy: 
  reserved_replicas: 10
  min_replicas: 4
  burst_replicas: 4
  burst_window_sec: 900  # 15min per burst slot
  kv_cache:
    enabled: true
    persistence: true
    ttl_hours: 12
  prewarm_schedule:
    - cron: "45 12 * * 1-5"  # prewarm 15m before market
      replicas: 12
  degrade_policy:
    queue_depth_threshold: 200
    sustained_sec: 60
    fallback_model: "redwood-compat-7b-quant"
```
Callout: real numbers to be tuned after bench. Also recommend on-call escalation hooks to SRE if queue depth > 300 for 120s.

morgan (Infra): Add to handoff: KMS smoke test step in prewarm job and a gating step preventing prewarm if KMS fails (prewarm should exit soft-fail and alert; do NOT proceed to full warm).

carlos (Sales Eng): Procurement note: include amortized note that warmup traffic is billed as normal inference; we can limit warmup size by targeting high-frequency prefixes only. Show worst-case overage with 4x spike events/month.

anya (Solutions): I'll prepare procurement-facing price table with two scenarios (quantized vs fp16), explicit line for burst credits, and a separate prewarm-run cost estimate. Also include a small paragraph explaining KV warmup billing.

vik (SRE): Action items: (1) SableBank to provide container + 20 prompts by EOD; (2) I will run perf bench and post results in this thread within 24h of receiving artifacts; (3) Anya to draft pricing table and runbook excerpt including KMS checklist; (4) Morgan to enumerate infra lead times and AZ placement trade-offs; (5) Carlos to prepare CFO-friendly one-pager noting worst-case scenarios.

security-bot: Security checklist: outstanding items - HSM integration test, SOC2 evidence, and vendor encryption attestation. All must be attached before Private deploy sign-off.

lena (AE): I'll push SableBank for the artifacts and confirm whether fallback to fp16 must be automated or just contractual. Re-open once perf numbers posted. Thanks team :thumbsup:

carlos (Sales Eng): Note for legal/procurement: if they require SLA 99.95 during market window, add +1-2 GPUs for active-active failover in AZs. Call that out in the CFO note.

anya (Solutions): Will include failover sizing and a short playbook for model downgrade.

lena (AE): Closing thread pending perf.
